issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java does not provide the expected public class Farm as described in the problem statement and shown by the solution. Instead the template declares a class named AnimalFarm and contains duplicated/embedded package and class declarations (syntax errors) which prevent compiling or implementing the intended Farm API (animals list, addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong). This structural mismatch between the problem description (which requires a Farm class) and the template will block students from completing the exercise and from using Main.java, which expects a Farm class.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java contents with a proper public class Farm in package de.tum.cit.ase that matches the specification: declare private List<Animal> animals, a no-argument constructor initializing animals as new ArrayList<>(), getters/setters, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), and singFarmSong()/private singFarmSongVerse(Animal). Remove the accidental duplicate package/class blocks and ensure the class name is Farm so Main.java and student code compile. Use the solution Farm.java as a reference structure while leaving method bodies as stubs/TODOs if desired for pedagogy.

issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java defines a class named AnimalFarm, while the problem statement and the solution use the class name Farm. This mismatch (file named Farm.java but class named AnimalFarm) breaks the direct conceptual mapping from the exercise description to the starter code, will confuse students (Main and instructions refer to Farm), and can cause compilation or lookup errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template file to Farm (public class Farm) so the class name matches the file name, the problem statement, and the solution. Ensure any references in Main or other starter code refer to Farm as well.
